title: Selling Pieces of Wood
summary: Given a rectangular piece of wood with dimensions m x n, and a list of prices for various rectangular pieces, determine the maximum revenue by cutting the wood into smaller pieces and selling them according to the given prices.
statement: Given a rectangular piece of wood with dimensions m x n, and a list of prices for various rectangular pieces, determine the maximum revenue by cutting the wood into smaller pieces and selling them according to the given prices. Each cut must be along the entire height or width, and the pieces cannot be rotated. You can sell multiple pieces of the same size and do not need to sell all possible sizes.
constraints: Start with one m by n rectangle and make any number of full horizontal or vertical cuts.
A listed [height,width,price] piece may be sold without rotation; unlisted pieces have direct price zero.
Return the maximum total sale value.
hints: Let dp[h][w] be the best value obtainable from that exact rectangle.
Initialize states with their best listed direct prices.
For every horizontal and vertical cut, combine the two resulting dp states and maximize.
The final operation of any optimal cutting plan is either no cut or one full cut into two independently optimal subrectangles, proving the recurrence.
editorial: The final operation of any optimal cutting plan is either no cut or one full cut into two independently optimal subrectangles, proving the recurrence.

tests.explanation: Combining profitable listed pieces through cuts yields maximum value nineteen.
Cutting into four unit pieces worth two each yields eight, which beats selling the whole piece for seven.
